clinician.trajectory_summary: A previously healthy 3-year-old girl presented with a 5-day history of right-sided cheek and eye swelling and pain accompanied by green nasal discharge. Initial examination revealed diffuse erythematous swelling refractory to oral antibiotics for suspected periorbital cellulitis. Imaging (MRI and cranial imaging) revealed a large, predominantly right-sided nasopharyngeal tumor with extension into ethmoid sinuses, orbits causing medial rectus muscle distortion, infratemporal fossa, pterygoid muscles, anterior and middle cranial fossae, and skull base destruction. Clinical progression included development of symptoms such as possible squint, mastication pain, and nasal breathing difficulty, indicating local invasion. A biopsy of the nasopharyngeal mass was ordered to obtain histopathological confirmation, which subsequently confirmed the diagnosis of non-metastatic parameningeal rhabdomyosarcoma.
